name: Courtney Bangs

bio.statement: Oregon Capital Chronicle's 2026 primary voter guide describes Bangs as a Clatsop County commissioner.
bio.excerpt: Courtney Bangs is a Clatsop County commissioner endorsed by Weber.

source.publisher: Oregon Capital Chronicle

bio.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, Bangs lists her occupation as substitute teacher, with a background as an academic director, teacher, dance instructor and agriculture education teacher.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Substitute Teacher Occupational Background: Academic Director; Teacher; Dance Instructor; Agriculture Education Teacher; FFA Advisor

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 40

bio.statement: Bangs lists a master's in agriculture education and a bachelor's in animal science from Oregon State University.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: Master's in Agriculture Education & Bachelor's in Animal Science at OSU

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 40

bio.statement: Bangs lists Clatsop County commissioner as her prior governmental experience.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Clatsop County Commissioner

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 40

positions.statement: In a July 2025 Daily Astorian article announcing her campaign, Bangs said rural communities have given a large environmental commitment on behalf of the state.
positions.excerpt: I feel like our communities have given a giant environmental commitment for the entire state

source.publisher: The Daily Astorian

positions.statement: Bangs says she has backed law enforcement.
positions.excerpt: I’ve followed through on my promises to back law enforcement

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 40

positions.statement: Bangs says she worked to end the childcare desert working families faced.
positions.excerpt: end the childcare desert working families faced

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 40

positions.statement: Bangs says she worked to stop the $4.3 billion gas tax.
positions.excerpt: stop Tina Kotek's $4.3 billion gas tax

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 40

positions.statement: Bangs says she has pushed back against state regulations that she says slow job creation and housing development.
positions.excerpt: While the politicians in Salem have pushed regulations that kill jobs and slow housing development, I've continued to fight back

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 40
